Pinza Triestina

Large Trieste sweet yeast bread enriched with butter, eggs, citrus, vanilla, sweet wine, and anise.

Yield: 3 large or 4 small loaves

Ingredients

about 16 2/3 cups strong bread flour, divided
3 cups granulated sugar, divided
about 8 large eggs
1 1/3 cups plus 1 tbsp butter, divided
about 1 2/3 cups fresh yeast
about 1/2 cup egg yolks, divided
about 1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp sweet wine or Marsala-rum mixture infused with anise seeds
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp whole milk, plus 1 tbsp for brushing
5 tsp fine salt
finely grated zest of 1 lemon
finely grated zest of 1 orange
seeds from 1 vanilla bean
1 egg yolk for brushing

Preparation

1. For the first dough, warm a large mixing bowl slightly.

2. Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk.

3. Add about 3 1/3 cups flour and 1/2 cup sugar.

4. Mix until uniform.

5. Cover.

6. Let rise until doubled.

7. For the second dough, beat 1/2 cup sugar with part of the egg yolks and about 4 whole eggs.

8. Add the lemon and orange zest.

9. Add the vanilla.

10. Add about 5 tbsp melted and cooled butter.

11. Add the flavored wine.

12. Mix in about 5 cups flour.

13. Add the first dough.

14. Beat vigorously until large bubbles form.

15. Cover.

16. Let rise again until doubled.

17. Put the remaining flour on the work surface.

18. Add the remaining whole eggs and yolks.

19. Add the remaining sugar.

20. Add the salt.

21. Melt the remaining butter.

22. Gradually work it in along with the second dough.

23. Knead by hand for at least 1 hour, until smooth, soft, and no longer sticky.

24. Divide into 3 or 4 portions.

25. Shape into round loaves.

26. Put on parchment-lined baking sheets.

27. Brush lightly with any remaining melted butter.

28. Cover.

29. Let rise in a warm place for about 3 hours.

30. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

31. Beat the finishing yolk with 1 tablespoon milk.

32. Brush the loaves.

33. Cut a deep star-shaped slash into each top.

34. Bake for about 45–50 minutes.

35. Check that the centers are fully baked.

36. Cool on a rack.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

The long final kneading develops enough structure to support this exceptionally rich butter-, sugar-, and egg-heavy dough.

South Tyrolean torn sweet pancake served with apple compote and lingonberry preserves.

5 large eggs
2 1/2 cups whole milk
1 pinch fine salt
4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
4 tbsp butter for cooking
1/4 cup powdered sugar
4 tbsp apple compote
4 tbsp lingonberry preserves

Preparation

1. Put the eggs in a large bowl.

2. Add the milk and salt.

3. Whisk until foamy.

4. Gradually add the flour.

5. Mix until no lumps remain.

6. Melt half of the butter in a large skillet.

7. Pour in half of the batter.

8. Cook over medium-low heat until the bottom is golden.

9. Turn the pancake.

10. Cook the second side.

11. Tear into irregular pieces with two spatulas.

12. Continue tossing until browned on all sides.

13. Transfer to a platter.

14. Repeat with the remaining butter and batter.

15. Dust with powdered sugar.

Service

Serve hot with apple compote and lingonberry preserves on the side.

Cooking in two batches prevents the pancake from becoming too thick and lets the torn pieces brown evenly.

South Tyrolean spiral fritters flavored with grappa, vanilla, and lemon.

Yield: about 8 fritters

Ingredients

2 cups plus 1 tbsp all-purpose flour
2 heaping tsp baking powder
1 pinch fine salt
3 large eggs
1 1/2 tbsp melted butter
scant 1/2 cup whole milk
scant 1/2 cup beer
2 tbsp grappa
1 tbsp vanilla extract
finely grated zest of 1 organic lemon
about 6 1/2 cups frying oil
1/3 cup powdered sugar
about 2/3 cup lingonberry preserves

Preparation

1. Sift the flour, baking powder, and salt into a large bowl.

2. Add the eggs.

3. Add the melted butter.

4. Add the milk.

5. Whisk.

6. Gradually add the beer.

7. Continue whisking until smooth.

8. Add the grappa, vanilla, and lemon zest.

9. Rest the batter for 10 minutes.

10. Heat the oil to 350°F in a wide deep skillet.

11. Fill a funnel dispenser with one ladleful of batter.

12. Let the batter stream into the oil in a continuous spiral.

13. Fry for 1 minute.

14. Turn with two slotted spoons.

15. Continue until the second side is golden.

16. Drain on paper towels.

17. Repeat with the remaining batter.

18. Dust with powdered sugar.

Service

Serve hot with lingonberry preserves.

Chef's note

Hold the funnel close to the oil surface to create an even spiral without breaking the batter stream.

17. Fry the second side until golden.

18. Drain on paper towels.

19. Dust with powdered sugar.

Spooning hot oil over the top while the first side cooks helps the krapfen puff properly.

Yield: 12 servings

Ingredients

For the sponge cake
2 cups all-purpose flour
1 1/4 cups granulated sugar
8 large eggs
1/2 cup plus 1 tbsp potato starch
1 tbsp butter for the pan
2 tbsp flour for the pan

For the pastry cream
4 egg yolks
2 cups plus 2 tbsp whole milk
1/2 cup plus 2 tbsp granulated sugar
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp all-purpose flour
peel of 1/2 lemon

For the chocolate cream
4 egg yolks
2 cups plus 2 tbsp whole milk
1/2 cup plus 2 tbsp granulated sugar
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp all-purpose flour
about 1 cup chopped dark chocolate

For the almond cream
1 1/2 cups toasted ground blanched almonds
3/4 cup granulated sugar
scant 1/2 cup water

For the royal icing
2 egg whites
1 1/2 cups powdered sugar
2 tsp lemon juice

For the rum syrup
1/3 cup rum
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp coffee
2 tbsp plus 2 tsp water
2 tsp granulated sugar

For the Alchermes syrup
1/3 cup Alchermes
2 tbsp water
1 tsp granulated sugar

For decorating
1/3 cup sliced almonds
1/4 cup colored sprinkles

Preparation

1. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

2. Butter and flour a roughly 12-inch cake pan.

3. Beat the 8 eggs with the sugar for at least 15–20 minutes.

4. Sift together the flour and potato starch.

5. Fold them in gently.

6. Pour into the pan.

7. Bake for about 45 minutes without opening the oven during the first 35 minutes.

8. Test with a toothpick.

9. Cool completely.

10. For the pastry cream, beat 4 yolks with the sugar and flour.

11. Heat the milk with the lemon peel.

12. Remove the peel.

13. Gradually whisk the hot milk into the yolk mixture.

14. Cook over low heat, stirring, until thick.

15. Transfer to a bowl and cool covered directly on the surface.

16. For the chocolate cream, repeat with the remaining yolks, milk, sugar, and flour.

17. At the end of cooking, add the chopped chocolate.

18. Stir until melted.

19. Cool covered directly on the surface.

20. For the almond cream, bring the water and sugar to a boil.

21. Gradually add the almonds.

22. Cook, stirring, until soft and slightly grainy.

23. Cool.

24. Mix the rum-syrup ingredients in one bowl.

25. Mix the Alchermes-syrup ingredients in another bowl.

26. Cut the sponge into 3 equal layers.

27. Moisten the first layer with the rum syrup.

28. Spread with chocolate cream.

29. Spread the almond cream over it.

30. Add the second layer.

31. Moisten with Alchermes syrup.

32. Spread with pastry cream.

33. Moisten the inner side of the third layer with Alchermes.

34. Place it upside down on the cake.

35. Moisten the top with the rum syrup.

36. Cover.

37. Refrigerate for at least 12 hours.

38. For the icing, beat the egg whites with the lemon juice.

39. Gradually add the powdered sugar.

40. Continue until smooth and firm.

41. Cover the entire cake.

42. Decorate with the sliced almonds and sprinkles.

43. Let the icing set before serving.

Service

Serve cold.

Chef's note

The overnight rest allows the syrups and three creams to balance and makes the cake easier to slice cleanly.

Parrozzo

Abruzzo semolina-and-almond cake flavored with citrus and coated in dark chocolate.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

1 1/4 cups granulated sugar
1 1/4 cups skin-on almonds
1 cup semolina
6 large eggs
finely grated zest of 1 lemon or orange
2 tbsp amaretto liqueur
about 2/3 cup chopped dark chocolate
2 tsp butter for the mold
1 tbsp semolina for the mold

Preparation

1. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

2. Butter a hemispherical parrozzo mold.

3. Dust it with semolina.

4. Finely grind the almonds.

5. Mix them with the semolina.

6. Separate the egg yolks and whites.

7. Beat the yolks with the sugar until pale and fluffy.

8. Beat the whites to stiff peaks.

9. Add the almonds and semolina to the yolks.

10. Add the citrus zest.

11. Add the amaretto.

12. Mix.

13. Gently fold in the egg whites in several additions.

14. Pour into the mold.

15. Bake for about 45 minutes.

16. Test with a toothpick.

17. Cool slightly.

18. Unmold.

19. Cool completely.

20. Chop the chocolate.

21. Melt it over a water bath.

22. Pour it over the cake.

23. Spread evenly over the entire surface.

24. Let the coating set.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Apply the chocolate coating only after the cake is completely cool.

Abruzzo Bocconotti

Castel Frentano pastries made with olive-oil shortcrust and a chocolate-almond filling.

Yield: about 30 pastries

Ingredients

For the filling
about 2 2/3 cups chopped dark chocolate
1 1/2 cups granulated sugar
about 2 3/4 cups toasted chopped almonds
1 pinch ground cinnamon
8 egg yolks
4 1/4 cups water

For the pastry
1 1/2 cups granulated sugar
15 egg yolks
1 cup plus 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
about 7 cups all-purpose flour

For the molds and finishing
3 tbsp lard
1/3 cup powdered sugar

Preparation

1. For the filling, heat the water in a large saucepan.

2. Add the chocolate and sugar.

3. Bring to a boil while stirring.

4. Turn off the heat.

5. Cool until warm.

6. Add the 8 egg yolks.

7. Return to the heat.

8. Bring to a boil again, stirring constantly.

9. Add the toasted chopped almonds.

10. Cook until thick enough to hold its shape.

11. Add the cinnamon.

12. Cool completely.

13. For the pastry, put the 15 yolks and sugar in a large bowl.

14. Beat until fluffy.

15. Add the olive oil.

16. Gradually add about 4 cups flour.

17. Transfer to a work surface.

18. Add more flour little by little until soft but no longer sticky.

19. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

20. Grease bocconotto molds with the lard.

21. Roll small thin pastry disks.

22. Line the bottoms and sides of the molds.

23. Fill each about two-thirds full.

24. Cover with a second pastry disk.

25. Seal the edges.

26. Arrange the molds on a baking sheet.

27. Bake for about 25 minutes, until golden.

28. Unmold while still warm.

29. Cool.

30. Dust with powdered sugar.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Add the flour gradually so the pastry does not become tougher than necessary.

Ferratelle

Abruzzo patterned wafers cooked in the traditional engraved iron and flavored with lemon.

Yield: about 20 wafers

Ingredients

2 medium eggs, room temperature
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp granulated sugar
1/4 cup neutral oil
1 2/3 cups all-purpose flour
finely grated zest of 1 lemon
1/3 tsp fine salt
1 1/2 tbsp melted butter for greasing the iron

Preparation

1. Put the eggs in a bowl.

2. Add the sugar.

3. Beat until uniform.

4. Add the oil.

5. Add the lemon zest.

6. Add the salt.

7. Gradually mix in the flour.

8. Mix into a soft but substantial dough.

9. Cover.

10. Rest at room temperature for 20–30 minutes.

11. Heat the ferratelle iron thoroughly.

12. Dip a piece of paper towel in the melted butter.

13. Lightly grease both plates.

14. Put a small portion of dough in the center of the iron.

15. Close.

16. Cook over low heat for 1–2 minutes.

17. Turn the iron.

18. Cook another 1–2 minutes, until evenly golden.

19. Open the iron.

20. Transfer the wafer to a rack.

21. Repeat with the remaining dough, regreasing only when needed.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Use only a small amount of dough because it spreads rapidly to the edges when the iron closes.

Abruzzo Cicerchiata

Abruzzo Carnival sweet made from tiny fried dough pieces bound with honey, sugar, and almonds.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

For the dough
4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
6 large eggs
6 tbsp granulated sugar
6 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
6 cups peanut oil for frying

For assembling
1 2/3 cups honey
2 tbsp granulated sugar
about 2/3 cup sliced blanched almonds
1/3 cup colored sprinkles

Preparation

1. Mound the flour on a work surface and make a well.
2. Add the eggs, sugar, and olive oil.
3. Knead vigorously until smooth and uniform.
4. Cover and rest for at least 30 minutes.
5. Divide the dough into pieces.
6. Roll into ropes about 3/8 inch thick.
7. Cut into pieces about 3/8 inch long.
8. Heat the peanut oil to 350°F.
9. Fry only a few pieces at a time until golden.
10. Drain on paper towels.
11. Put the honey and sugar in a large saucepan.
12. Heat over medium heat until the sugar dissolves and the honey is very fluid.
13. Add the fried pieces and almonds.
14. Stir quickly until everything is coated.
15. Transfer to a lightly dampened platter or ring mold.
16. Shape the cicerchiata.
17. Decorate immediately with sprinkles.
18. Cool completely.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Work quickly during assembly because the honey thickens rapidly as it cools.
